subject: Orbital: final commercial remediation & governance ask
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Jake Turner <jake.turner@orbital.systems>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Legal - Orbital <legal@orbital.systems>
Date: Sat, 25 Feb 2028 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Orbital: commercial remediation proposal and next steps

Jake — thanks again for the candor on Friday. I wanted to follow up with a concise proposal so we can close the remediation conversation and get your team the operational guarantees you need.

Summary of impact (Redwood findings):
- 2028-02-24 02:10–03:40 UTC: sustained 5xx spike on the prod inference cluster servicing orbital-prod leading to ~18% error-rate vs normal <0.5%.
- 2028-02-24 02:45–04:15 UTC: throughput dropped by ~45% for requests >1024 tokens due to an interaction between recent kernel selector changes and your request shape.
- Average tail latency for priority routes rose from 180ms to 840ms during the event.

What we propose (commercial + governance):
1) One-time commercial credit: 20% of March committed monthly run-rate (CMR) applied to your March invoice; modeled on the observed SLO breach window and sustained impact. Details in attached proposed-credit-workback.xlsx.
2) Technical remediation deliverables: immediate kernel rollback for your dedicated pool (completed), plus a targeted optimization deployment next week with Canary for long sequence traffic.
3) Governance & acceptance: 30-day joint post-mortem, weekly checkpoints for two cycles, and a SLA addendum that narrows the committed lat/throughput SLOs and defines a faster escalation path.

Attachments: sla_metrics_q1.csv (metrics slice), redwood-diagnostics-20280224.tgz (logs + traces), proposed-credit-workback.xlsx (calculation basis).

Request: please confirm by EOD Mon whether the proposed credit + governance package is acceptable to Orbital. If Legal needs edits, we can route a short addendum via DocuSign for signature.

Thanks — Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0126
[Attachment: sla_metrics_q1.csv (CSV)]
[Attachment: redwood-diagnostics-20280224.tgz (tar.gz)]
From: Jake Turner <jake.turner@orbital.systems>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Alyssa Grant <alyssa.grant@orbital.systems>, Legal - Orbital <legal@orbital.systems>
Date: Mon, 27 Feb 2028 09:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Orbital: commercial remediation proposal and next steps

Naomi — thanks for the write-up. A few quick points from Orbital leadership:

- The outage window you described impacted our customer-facing recommender during a busy batch run and directly caused missed SLAs for two enterprise customers. This is material.
- 20% of CMR is a start but is likely insufficient given downstream revenue exposure. We also need a formal indemnity for any recurring regressions and a binding timeline for the fixes.

Can you provide:
1) A clear calendar for the optimization deployment (dates/times and expected rollback plan).
2) A more aggressive credit construct or an option to convert the credit into a service-days extension or enhanced support hours for Q2.
3) A short draft of the SLA addendum we can share with Legal this week.

I want to resolve this without an escalation to our board, but we need reassurance. I’m available for a 30-min exec-to-exec on Tue if that helps.

-Jake
Jake Turner
VP Product, Orbital Systems
jake.turner@orbital.systems | +1 (617) 555-4421
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 27 Feb 2028 10:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Orbital: commercial remediation proposal and next steps

Looping internal stakeholders with a recommended counterproposal for Jake: we should land fast and avoid public escalation. Proposed edits below — I’ll own the exec sync if Naomi wants to sit in.

Sales recommended counterproposal (high level):
- Maintain the 20% one-time credit option, and also offer an alternate package: 10% credit + 40 hours of premium on-call engineering support (dedicated hours) during March–April for targeted workload tuning.
- If Orbital prefers an invoice credit, allow conversion to enhanced support via a single email confirmation (no renegotiation).
- Add an SLA addendum draft that includes a 48-hour emergency escalation path to our on-call principal engineer and a 5-business-day remediation commitment for regressions that can be traced to Redwood deployment changes.

Technical clarifications for the exec call: Vivek — please confirm the exact schedule for the optimization rollout and the Canary gating criteria. Evelyn — please pull the downstream customer incident list so Legal and Jake can see impacted accounts and severity.

I’ll prepare a short slide with the two commercial options and the addendum draft for Legal.

-Ben
[Attachment: proposed-credit-workback.xlsx (XLSX)]
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Feb 2028 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Orbital: commercial remediation proposal and next steps

Ben/Naomi — technical plan and schedule:
- Today (28 Feb): full rollback of kernel selector changes for Orbital's dedicated pool — completed at 02:30 PT. Monitoring shows error-rate returning to baseline for standard requests.
- Thu, 01 Mar (22:00–02:00 UTC): targeted optimization deployment in canary with 10% of long-sequence traffic (gated). If canary passes 6h stability and perf checks we promote to 50% over 2 hours and then full.
- Rollback plan: immediate feature-flag disable and automated traffic drain; will revert state and restore previous kernels within 15 minutes in the worst case.

Canary gating criteria: 5xx < 0.7% sustained, p99 latency < 350ms for priority routes, throughput within 90% of baseline.

I’ll join the exec sync Tue 09:30 PT to walk through the gating and safety nets.

-Vivek
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-diagnostics-20280224.tgz (logs)]
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Jake Turner <jake.turner@orbital.systems>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Legal - Orbital <legal@orbital.systems>
Date: Thu, 1 Mar 2028 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Orbital: commercial remediation proposal and next steps — proposed next steps and DocuSign

Jake — thanks for the quick reply and for agreeing to the exec touchpoint. Per our call this morning:

Agreed commercial path (two options for you to choose):
A) One-time 20% credit of March CMR applied to your March invoice (no extra work required).
B) One-time 10% credit + 40 hours of dedicated premium support (engineer hours during March–April) — Redwood will schedule the conjointed tuning blocks with your infra team.

You indicated you’ll confirm preference with Legal. I’ve asked our Legal team to prepare a short SLA addendum; the draft is uploaded to DocuSign for signature if you accept the credit path A or B as-is: https://docusign.net/link/ABC-ORBITAL-20280301

Operational timeline reminder: targeted canary deploy tonight at 22:00 UTC (see Vivek’s gating criteria). If the canary passes we’ll promote and close the remediation plan. We’ll run a joint post-mortem and submit the 30-day action plan.

Next steps: please confirm which commercial option you prefer so we can route DocuSign and close the case. If Legal requests changes to the addendum, flag them here and we will triage.

Appreciate the collaboration — Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: proposed-credit-workback.xlsx (XLSX)]
